dialogue.text: Naa doom jotna yi tang? Wone jokk seeral jikkoo.

dialogue.text: Dama fenk ci genn yàgg jigeen ak xale ci sàmm liggéey yi.

dialogue.speaker: B

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Jám naañu ci ndokk bi, yàppam ci ci sàccu moom teere wi?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Fokki am nañu fi yàpp, liggéeyam moom bés ba xët bi nekk.
dialogue.translation: We must have a solution here, start working on it before the rainy season arrives.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Ñu xam ci sàbb gi, réewum bës ak kër gi, ñu dëgg ci ñu am yàpp.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Jám naa leen wone ci ci yàppam bi, moom am nañu ci teere wi.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Am nañu moom fi yàpp, liggéey ci teere wi, ñu dëgg ci ñu yépp.
dialogue.translation: We have solutions here, let's work within this theory, so they can all see.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sàccu leen ci teere wi, jám naa leen wone ci ñu am yàpp?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Bés ci liggéeyam, leen am nañu yàpp, ñu dëgg ci ñu jëm ci réewum.
dialogue.translation: Before starting work, they need solutions so they can move forward in their countries.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Xam naa leen sàbb gi, ci sàccu ci teere wi, ñu am yàppam.
dialogue.translation: I know the reason for this, by adopting this theory, they will have solutions.

dialogue.translation: Us, how often do we accept women as part of the share?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Yàñ yu bés wàllu jëf ci bokk lanu bëgg. Ñun, man ñuumte lañu bëgg ci wàllu baar.
dialogue.translation: We can accept them when it’s a part we want. We, our plan is to want stability.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Ndaxte ñu baar ci jigéen bokk? Am naa ci jigéen yàggale ba noppi.
dialogue.translation: Why worry about women’s shares? I see women hesitating more now.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Bëgg naa wàllu jëf ci bokk, man ndaxte am naa ci baar.
dialogue.translation: I want to be able to accept the share, but I also have concerns.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Ñun, ñuumte lanu la ñu baral ci baar yàñ yu bés.
dialogue.translation: Our plan should balance work time and stability concerns.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Wàllu bëgg naa ci yàñ yu bés, ndaxte ndaxte ba noppi ñu baar.
dialogue.translation: We can want stability in our work time, but why worry about it now?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Ndaxte yaw bokk lañu la jéem ci jigéen? Man ñu baar ci bokk lanu la.
dialogue.translation: Why do we hesitate to include women in the share? I worry about their part too.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Ñun, ñuumte lanu la ba noppi ba ñu jëf ci bokk.
dialogue.translation: Our plan now is to accept the share as it comes.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Nanga defar ndogal ci demokaraasi? Baa ngi jëfandikoo yëngu ndogal laa bëgg?
dialogue.translation: How is power structured in a democracy? I like that power changes frequently, right?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Demokaraasi laa di xam, ci mbir yàq sàcc. Ndey, ngoon laa bëgg ci demokaraasi laa jox ci mbir sàccu ci mbir ndogal.
dialogue.translation: I know about democracy, with very strict laws. But I prefer a democracy where power is granted within legal frameworks.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Lu jot laa bëgg ci demokaraasi? Defar ndogal jot laa di wax, ci mbir yàq sàcc.
dialogue.translation: What do you prefer in democracy? I say power should be divided in many ways, with strict laws.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Dara laa bëgg ci mbir demokaraasi. Làkka ngi leen jëm ci mbir ndogal jot, waxe ci mbir sàccu.
dialogue.translation: I don't like anything in how democracy works. So that power can be shared among different groups, based on laws.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Wàll demokaraasi laa di wax! Ndey, ci mbir ndogal jot laa di wone ci sàccu yàq.
dialogue.translation: I'm advocating for democracy! But I see that in decentralized power, laws are very strict.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Nanga defu ndogal ci demokaraasi? Ci mbir sàccu laa di wone ci mbir kàll jot.
dialogue.translation: How is power structured in a democracy? I see it in legal frameworks, from different perspectives.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Lu mu ngi wax ci mbir demokaraasi? Sàccu jot laa doon di jox ci mbir ndogal.
dialogue.translation: What do they say about democracy? I would grant different laws based on power distribution.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Ñunga wax ci mbir demokaraasi laa di wone ci mbir kàll jot. Sàccu laa di wone ci mbir ndogal.
dialogue.translation: They talk about democracy from different angles. I see laws in relation to power distribution.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Dama ko ci kàlla ci rew yàgg, fàtt yemb ci liggéey, yàq?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Waa, dom ci ci Sénégal, rew leen yëngu agsi ci liggéey ga, dom dàq ci kàll ciw.
dialogue.translation: Yes, but in Senegal, people usually help each other in work, but not in all areas.

dialogue.text: Ko bokk ci ci ngirëm sèdd ci liggéey, leen agsi ci liggéey ga, dom mënul yàgg ci ci mbirum.
